title: Symmetric monoidal structure transported along an ordinary equivalence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category], and let $E:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:H$ be an equivalence with specified natural unit and counit isomorphisms $\eta:\mathrm{id}\cong HE$, $\epsilon:EH\cong\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the triangle identities. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is monoidal [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and symmetric: it has a natural braiding $\beta_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$ satisfying both hexagons and $\beta_{Y,X}\beta_{X,Y}=\mathrm{id}$. Then the bifunctor
$$X\diamond Y=E(HX\otimes HY),\qquad f\diamond g=E(Hf\otimes Hg)$$
and unit $E\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ admit the transported symmetric monoidal structure. With its canonical comparisons, $E$ and $H$ are strong symmetric monoidal [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], and $\eta,\epsilon$ are monoidal natural isomorphisms. The transported braiding is $E(\beta_{HX,HY})$.

Its monoidal structure is CategoryTheory.Monoidal.transport at Transport.lean:162, whose data are transportStruct at :138–155, giving exactly the stated tensor, unit and braiding. The same chosen equivalence is equivalenceTransported at :196. The inverse/forward Monoidal instances are :198 and :205, and unit/counit IsMonoidal instances :217 and :221. Braided/Transport.lean:39 and :67 give inverse/forward Braided instances, so these strong monoidal functors are symmetric.
